The complete graph is then traversed by `serialized_len_capped` at lines 491–493. Only afterward does `admit_canonical_privacy` charge `4 * serialized_bytes + truth_rows` at lines 511–515; its first observer event is even later, at lines 527–538.

The existing 512 KiB test proves the flaw: [validate.rs:725](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/tests/architecture/evidence/validate.rs:725) runs with `canonical_prefix_work - 1`. Control flow fully serializes the long graph at production line 491 and then fails at line 515. The asserted `[0,0,0]` phase count merely means the late observer did not fire; it does not mean no traversal occurred. This exact test passed on ARM in 0.92 seconds.

The `4 * serialized_bytes` oracle is also not derived from the implementation’s passes. `validate_canonical` serializes, clones, serializes the clone again, then privacy validation performs `serde_json::to_vec`, scans that buffer, parses each string, and revalidates it ([fact.rs:433](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/schema/fact.rs:433), [identity.rs:379](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/schema/identity.rs:379)). A long-label-dominated graph therefore receives more than four asymptotic full-content passes after admission, besides the pre-admission sizing pass.

Minimal R10 contract: obtain raw string/field lengths using O(1) `.len()` operations under an admitted container traversal, then charge the existing `ProjectionBudget` before any serialization, cloning, hashing, privacy scan, or observer visit. Derive an explicit conservative pass bound, with an independent long-label oracle and a pre-admission visitor counter.

### 2. HIGH — the capped serializer does not cap work on long strings; SCC and cycle charges remain length-blind

`serialized_len_capped` only limits calls reaching `CountingWriter` ([hash.rs:7](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/hash.rs:7), lines 98–101). Pinned `serde_json 1.0.149` scans an entire unescaped string before calling `write_string_fragment`. Thus:

```text
serialized_len_capped(&"p".repeat(1 MiB), 1)
```

writes the opening quote, scans all 1 MiB looking for escapes, and only then reaches the writer and fails. The existing cap test uses an element-by-element sequence ([hash.rs:24](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/tests/architecture/hash.rs:24)); it cannot expose this string behavior.

The same defect remains in the graph phases:

- SCC charges only `5V + 6E` before serialization and variable-length edge identity rehashing ([scc.rs:358](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/project/scc.rs:358), lines 385 and 440).
- Cycle domain charges only `V + 3E` before serialization and identity validation ([cycle.rs:52](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/project/cycle.rs:52), lines 74 and 88).
- Member hashing charges only `members.len()` before serializing variable-length identities ([cycle.rs:791](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/project/cycle.rs:791)).

Concrete bounded counterexample: `CanonicalText` permits a 1 MiB value ([identity.rs:279](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/schema/identity.rs:279)). A singleton SCC with a short key and one with a 1 MiB key both receive SCC work `5`; a two-node/four-edge cycle receives domain work `14` and member-hash work `2` in both forms, despite megabytes of additional comparisons, clones, serializer scans, and hashes.

Minimal R10 contract: replace writer-only work limiting with a serializer/preflight layer that charges source string bytes before serde_json escape scanning. Cover long unescaped, late-escape, escape-heavy, one-below, and arithmetic-overflow cases. SCC/cycle phase work must include serialized/raw identity lengths, not only cardinalities.

### 3. HIGH — a public graph-kernel identity entrypoint bypasses budget ownership entirely

[ComponentIdentity::validate_members at scc.rs:154](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/project/scc.rs:154) is public, accepts no `ProjectionBudget`, has no count or byte limit, and calls `hash_serialized`. That helper uses full-buffer `serde_json::to_vec` ([hash.rs:90](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/hash.rs:90)).

Counterexample: call it with an arbitrary-length slice of valid 1 MiB virtual identities and any forged digest. It allocates and hashes the complete serialization before returning the inevitable digest mismatch. This path is also invoked from the credited inner validator, so it is not an outer-validation finding.

Minimal R10 contract: make this method non-public and callable only with an admission token produced from the same caller-owned `ProjectionBudget`, or accept that budget directly and precharge member count, content work, and capped streaming-hash bytes. No replacement budget may be minted.

### 4. MEDIUM — cycle basis allocation is under-reserved; the exact-prefix test overfits rank four

`admit_basis_search_bytes` reserves exactly `target * size_of::<CycleWitness>()` and exactly one `usize` per edge ([cycle.rs:820](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/src/architecture/project/cycle.rs:820)). Production instead creates `witnesses` with `Vec::new()` at line 512 and pushes at lines 649–650. On the pinned ARM toolchain, a moderate-sized element’s first `Vec` allocation has capacity four.

The already-linked non-triangle fixture returns rank three and three witnesses ([cycle.rs:140](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/tests/architecture/project/cycle.rs:140)); it passed on ARM. Its `Vec<CycleWitness>` therefore allocates four slots while only three are reserved. Its six sparse `outgoing` buckets also each allocate at least four `usize` slots at production lines 504–509, while admission reserves only the eight logical edge slots. BTreeMap node allocations are omitted as well.

The R9 prefix test uses only the six-edge triangle with rank four ([cycle.rs:394](/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-lang/xtask/tests/architecture/project/cycle.rs:394)), masking the output-vector capacity rounding. Production-derived `bytes_reserved` and self-emitted phase events are not independent allocation oracles.

Minimal R10 contract: use `try_reserve_exact`/`Vec::with_capacity(target)` for output, use packed adjacency with exact audited capacity or reserve actual per-bucket rounded capacities, and account for map/set nodes. Add allocator-observed rank-3 and sparse one-outgoing-edge fixtures; one byte below each phase delta must fail before the real allocation, without borrowing slack from earlier over-reservations.

## Smallest clean-break API

Do not introduce a large cross-crate framework. Four breaking boundaries suffice:

```rust
#[must_use]
pub struct Failure<R, K> {
    pub kind: K,
    pub report: R,
}

pub trait Scheduler<N, A> {
    fn run(
        &self,
        graph: &mut EGraph<N, A>,
        rules: &[&dyn RewriteFn<N, A>],
    ) -> Result<SaturationReport, Failure<SaturationReport, SaturationStop>>;
}

pub enum SaturationStop {
    IterationLimit,
    NodeLimit,
    GrowthLimit,
    Timeout,
    Cancelled,
    PropagationUnsatisfiable,
}
```

`SaturationReport` should replace contradictory booleans with one stop reason and always contain initial/final nodes/classes, iterations, applied rules, configured/observed budgets, elapsed/cancel state, and per-rule counts. Only fixed point is `Ok`.

```rust
pub fn extract_roots(
    graph: &EGraph<...>,
    roots: &[(RuleId, Id)],
    cost: &impl CostModel<...>,
    budget: ExtractionBudget,
) -> Result<ExtractionPlan, Failure<ExtractionReport, ExtractionError>>;

pub enum ExtractionError {
    MissingRoot { rule: RuleId },
    MissingBest { class: Id },
    MissingChild { parent: Id, child: Id },
    Cycle { path: Vec<Id> },
    Limit,
    Timeout,
    NonFiniteCost { class: Id },
}
```

Remove public semantic use of `best_node -> Option` and the recursive `Option` materializers. Use gray/black visitation so sharing is distinct from a cycle.

```rust
pub fn optimize_grammar(
    input: &GrammarIR,
    budget: OptimizationBudget,
) -> Result<GrammarOptimization, GrammarOptimizationFailure>;

impl GrammarOptimization {
    pub fn commit(self, target: &mut GrammarIR) -> Result<OptimizationReport, TranslationFailure>;
}
```

`GrammarOptimization` owns every rule body and the final string pool together. Before one commit it validates input revision/fingerprint, exact root/rule cardinality, unique IDs, every child, every `StringId`/`FnId`/`RuleId`, complete extraction, and translation round-trip. No per-rule mutation, `filter_map`, `Epsilon` coercion, or separate pool write-back.

Finally, change search to a typed complete outcome:

```rust
pub fn solve_complete(
    &mut self,
    config: &SolveConfig,
) -> Result<ValidatedSolutions<D>, Failure<SolveReport, SolveStop>>;

pub enum SolveStop { Unsat, BudgetExceeded, Cancelled, Timeout, InvalidAssignment }
```

Best-so-far may appear in the error report for diagnostics but is not exposed as a publishable plan. `solve_grammar_components` builds component-local plans, independently validates complete assignments, and merges only after every component succeeds.

Smallest no-hook design: extract the existing transaction boundaries into production phase functions and make the one-shot solver compose them. Do not add observers, sleeps, threads, or a second solve API.

### Transaction refactor

In `crates/ir/src/passes/csp_strategy/solve.rs`, extract:

```rust
pub(super) fn enter_component(
    output: GrammarSolveOutput,
    root: RuleId,
    members: &[RuleId],
    config: &SolveConfig,
) -> Result<GrammarSolveOutput, OptimizationUnavailable>;

pub(super) fn commit_component(
    output: GrammarSolveOutput,
    component: ComponentOutput,
    config: &SolveConfig,
) -> Result<GrammarSolveOutput, OptimizationUnavailable>;

pub(super) fn finish_grammar_transaction(
    output: GrammarSolveOutput,
    config: &SolveConfig,
) -> Result<GrammarSolveOutput, OptimizationUnavailable>;
```

Then force `solve_grammar_components` through:

```rust
output = enter_component(output, root, members, &config)?;
let component = solve_component(...)?;
output = commit_component(output, component, &config)?;
...
finish_grammar_transaction(output, &config)
```

- `enter_component` owns the existing pre-component boundary report.
- `commit_component` checks the current token before merging either `FactorizedExact` or `Optimal` output, marks that report cancelled, and returns only `OptimizationUnavailable`.
- `finish_grammar_transaction` owns the final pre-return check.
- Remove the duplicated factorized/constrained post-decode checks at `solve.rs:512-518,545-551`; the common commit owns acceptance. Retain the solve-start and post-search checks because they guard different work intervals.
- Make `ComponentOutput` and only the required fields `pub(super)`, consistent with the existing externally attached tests. Do not expose any of this publicly.

External tests in `crates/ir/tests/passes/csp_strategy/mod.rs`:

- `factorized_component_is_rejected_if_cancelled_at_commit`
  - Construct a `ComponentOutput` with `FactorizedExact`, a nonempty objective, and sentinel maps.
  - Cancel immediately before `commit_component`.
  - Require `Err(Cancelled)`, one cancelled report, objective removed, and no output type.

- `cancellation_after_completed_component_stops_at_next_boundary`
  - Commit component 0 while uncancelled.
  - Cancel between calls.
  - Call `enter_component` for component 1.
  - Require reports `[component-0 completed, component-1 cancelled boundary]`.

- `cancellation_after_last_component_stops_final_grammar_commit`
  - Commit the last component while uncancelled.
  - Cancel before `finish_grammar_transaction`.
  - Require `Err(Cancelled)` and the last report rewritten to cancelled with no objective.

These are deterministic state transitions: the test flips the token between real production phases. They need no timing race or test-only callback. A public incremental transaction/state-machine API would be unnecessary authority expansion.

### Engine oracle

In `cross_rule_csp.rs:418-460`:

- Replace the `if let (Some, Some)` with two `expect` calls.
- Assert `engine_decisions.len() == 2`.
- Assert `solved.reports[0].constraints.engine > 0` before comparing engines.
- Remove the unused `dag` binding.

The fixture’s empty `regex_info` produces DFA-only domains, so engine propagation should be installed; `> 0` proves the test did not merely observe two independent equal minima.

### Partition oracle

Delete `collect_refs` and `reference_partition` from `cross_rule_csp.rs:110-167`. `partition_by_call_graph` is already public.

Use a tiny normalization wrapper around the production result and compare it to literal expected component sets. This tests production without copying its union-find algorithm. Also extend `crates/ir/tests/lattices/csp_components.rs` with one mixed fixture covering transitive, reverse-directed, nested-Ref, and isolated rules.

Avoid a second “independent” union-find implementation—it can reproduce the same dense-ID assumptions while never exercising production.

### Public compile oracle

The truly minimal repair is claim correction:

- Rename the current test to `optimizer_error_install_boundary_preserves_exact_variant_and_sidecars`.
- Say it dynamically proves the install boundary; public entrypoints are source/type-proved, not dynamically forced to fail.

If dynamic public propagation remains mandatory, the only hook-free route is a real caller feature: add `grammar_solve_control: GrammarSolveControl` to `PipelineOptions`, have the canonical pipeline pass it directly, and test `compile_grammar` with a pre-cancelled token. Keep the installer sentinel test separately.

That API expansion needs explicit policy approval: it weakens R3’s “production explicitly passes `cancel: None`” posture and broadens public compilation authority. A private injected closure would be smaller mechanically but would be a production test hook and should be rejected.

### Surgical mutants

M05 should delete only the final-token recheck:

```diff
- if csp.stats().cancelled || cancellation_requested(config) {
+ if csp.stats().cancelled {
```

`cancellation_on_final_singleton_leaf_discards_incumbent` then kills exactly that seam; pre-search stats behavior remains intact.

Split the combined M06 test into separately named tests. Use:

- `M06a-clamp-foreign-var-id`: change only the index calculation to clamp the foreign ID. `foreign_var_id_is_rejected` then observes an illicit `Ok`.
- If incomplete acceptance itself must be mutation-proved, add `M06b-synthesize-missing-assignment`: remove the solution-length guard and fill only a missing solution slot from the domain. `incomplete_solution_is_rejected` kills that one behavior.
- Do not bundle length deletion, foreign-ID clamping, missing-value synthesis, oversized input, and objective failures into one patch/test.

If the matrix must remain exactly seven specimens, use the one-line foreign-ID mutant as M06 and retain incomplete/oversized as independent baseline tests. If both counterfactuals are mandatory, treat M06a/M06b as two sub-specimens and acknowledge the extra execution rather than coupling them.

Main KISS risk: widening helpers merely for tests. Keep them `pub(super)`, make them the sole owners of code already present inline, and ensure the public one-shot path cannot bypass them.
